nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns confirm successful synthesis of CoP, Co, and Co₃O₄ materials with characteristic reflections.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns, X-ray adsorption near edge structure (XANES) spectra, and Fourier transform extended X-ray absorption fine structure (FT-EXAFS) spectra prove the successful synthesis of CoP, Co, and Co₃O₄ materials (Figure 1a-c).

nodes.characterization_summary: Normalized XANES spectra of Co K-edge show valence states for Co foil, CoP, Co, and Co₃O₄ with slight differences due to surface oxidation and thickness effects.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Normalized XANES spectra of Co K-edge over Co foil, CoP, Co, and Co₃O₄. The slight difference between the Co catalyst and Co foil in XANES spectra can be ascribed to the inevitable oxidation of Co and the thickness effects.

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-EXAFS spectra in R space confirm local coordination environments of CoP, Co, and Co₃O₄.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fourier transform extended X-ray absorption fine structure (FT-EXAFS) spectra prove the successful synthesis of CoP, Co, and Co₃O₄ materials (Figure 1a-c).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM images show thin amorphous shell formation on CoP surface after exposure to 1 M KOH for 1500 s.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) images show the appearance of a thin layer of amorphous shell on the surface of CoP and Co after exposure to 1 M KOH solution for 1500 s (Figures 1d and S3 and S4).

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES shows rapid dissolution of P and Co elements from CoP into KOH solution, stabilizing after 600 s with more P dissolution than Co.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectrometry (ICP-OES) displays the quick dissolution of Co and P elements into the solution and achieves stability in 600 s (Figure 1e).

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectra show Co(OH)₂ peaks at 502 and 688 cm⁻¹ for CoP and Co after KOH exposure, disappearing after pre-reduction at -0.6 V vs RHE; Co₃O₄ peaks remain constant.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Compared with the fresh samples, two new Raman peaks indexed to Co(OH)₂ (502 and 688 cm⁻¹) appear in CoP and Co after exposure to KOH solution... The constant Raman peak density and position of Co₃O₄ indicates the maintaining of Co₃O₄ species on the surface (Figure 1h).

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS confirms surface reconstruction sequence CoP → Co(OH)₂ → Co for CoP@Co; Co 2p Co⁰ binding energy 777.82 eV (CoP@Co) vs 777.94 eV (Co) indicates electron donation from CoP core.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) also confirms the surface conversion process from CoP to Co(OH)₂ during exposure to KOH solution and from Co(OH)₂ to Co during pre-reduction (Figure S5). ... the binding energy of Co⁰ peak in CoP@Co is 777.82 eV, lower than that of Co (777.94 eV) (Figure 6b).

nodes.characterization_summary: Intermittent in situ Raman shows alternating Co(OH)₂ peak appearance with NO₃⁻ addition at OCP and disappearance at +0.1 V vs RHE for CoP@Co; Co(OH)₂ disappears below -0.1 V vs RHE during NRA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The alternate appearance of Co(OH)₂ Raman peaks with the addition of a small amount of nitrate under open circuit potential (OCP) and the consumption of nitrate under +0.1 V vs RHE... The results show the disappearance of Co(OH)₂ for CoP@Co below -0.1 V vs RHE during NRA (Figure 4a).

nodes.characterization_summary: Electrochemical in situ XANES shows Co valence state of +1.22 for CoP@Co at 0 V vs RHE (between CoP +0.90 and Co(OH)₂ +2.00); +0.87 at -0.4 V vs RHE.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The nominal valence state of CoP@Co at 0 V vs RHE in electrolyte is +1.22, which locates between CoP (+0.90) and Co(OH)₂ (+2.00)... Under -0.4 V vs RHE, CoP@Co has a normalized valence state of +0.87 in electrochemical in situ XANES.

nodes.characterization_summary: *H₂O peak at 1650 cm⁻¹ for CoP@Co shifts to 1635 cm⁻¹ under high overpotential; peaks at 1280, 1357, 1450 cm⁻¹ indicate *NH₂, *NO, *NH₄⁺.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For CoP@Co, the *H₂O peak locates at 1650 cm⁻¹ under low overpotential, but shifts to a lower wavenumber (1635 cm⁻¹) under high overpotential... the FTIR peaks located at 1280 cm⁻¹, 1357 and 1450 cm⁻¹ indexes to *NH₂, *NO and *NH₄⁺, respectively (Figure 4d,e).

nodes.characterization_summary: H₂O-TPD shows *H₂O desorption peaks at 189°C for Co(OH)₂ and 226°C for Co; three peaks for Co(OH)₂ at 120°C, 189°C, 400-460°C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the H₂O temperature-programmed desorption (H₂O-TPD) profiles show three peaks for Co(OH)₂, corresponding to the desorption of water among particles (120°C), the desorption of *H₂O (189°C), and dehydration of structural hydroxides (400-460°C)... *H₂O desorption temperature over Co (226°C) is higher than that of Co(OH)₂ (189°C).

nodes.characterization_summary: Electrochemical quasi in situ EPR with DMPO shows stronger DMPO-H signal for CoP@Co than Co at -0.2 V vs RHE in 1 M KOH; signal weakens with NO₃⁻ addition.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The EPR spectra of CoP@Co and Co (in 1.0 M KOH solution at -0.2 V vs RHE) are recorded using 5,5-dimethyl-1-pyrroline-N-oxide (DMPO) as the H-radical trapping reagent (Figure 6d). The signal intensity of DMPO-H over CoP@Co is much stronger than that of Co.

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-NRA XRD patterns show no changes in bulk crystal structure, demonstrating structural durability of catalysts.
nodes.evidence_snippet: After the NRA test, XRD patterns show no changes, demonstrating the durability of the bulk crystal structure (Figures 2f and S13).
